s14-introduction-to-binary-search-tree.trick: A strict BST keeps every left-subtree value below its root and every right-subtree value above it. Its inorder traversal is sorted.
s14-introduction-to-binary-search-tree.space: O(h) call stack plus O(n) output

s14-search-in-a-binary-search-tree.trick: Compare with the current node: go left for smaller values and right for larger values.

s14-find-min-max-in-bst.trick: The leftmost node is minimum and the rightmost node is maximum in a nonempty BST.

s14-ceil-in-a-binary-search-tree.trick: Seek the smallest value at least x. When a node qualifies, remember it and look left for a closer answer.

s14-floor-in-a-binary-search-tree.trick: Seek the largest value at most x. When a node qualifies, remember it and look right for a closer answer.

s14-insert-a-given-node-in-binary-search.trick: Follow comparisons until reaching an empty child link and create the node there. This strict-BST version ignores duplicate values.

s14-delete-a-node-in-binary-search-tree.trick: Find the target by BST comparison. If it has two children, replace its value with its inorder successor, then remove that successor.

s14-find-k-th-smallest-largest-element-i.trick: Inorder yields ascending values and reverse inorder descending values. Stop after visiting k nodes rather than storing the full traversal.

s14-check-if-a-tree-is-a-bst-or-bt.trick: A node must lie strictly between bounds inherited from all its ancestors, not only be ordered against its immediate children.

s14-lca-in-binary-search-tree.trick: If both targets are below the current value, go left; if both are above, go right. The first split point is their LCA.

s14-construct-a-bst-from-a-preorder-trav.trick: Consume preorder once. Each recursive subtree accepts only values within its allowed lower and upper BST bounds.

s14-inorder-successor-predecessor-in-bst.trick: While searching for x, a smaller node is a predecessor candidate and a larger node is a successor candidate; move toward x for tighter bounds.

s14-merge-2-bst-s.trick: Maintain an inorder stack for each tree. Repeatedly take the smaller next value and advance only that tree.
s14-merge-2-bst-s.space: O(h₁ + h₂) stacks plus O(n + m) output

s14-two-sum-in-bst-check-if-there-exists.trick: Use one inorder iterator from the minimum and another in reverse from the maximum. Move the side that makes the sum approach the target.

s14-recover-bst-correct-bst-with-two-nod.trick: Morris inorder traversal detects out-of-order neighboring values while using temporary threads. The first wrong predecessor and last wrong current node are swapped.

s14-largest-bst-in-binary-tree.trick: For each subtree return its minimum, maximum, and size. It forms a BST only if its root exceeds the left maximum and is below the right minimum.
